subject.title: RFC: allow organization publishers to set a GitHub profile independent of their handle

question: Should ClawHub add owner- or admin-managed GitHub profile metadata for organization publishers, and should that value be a constrained GitHub handle rather than an arbitrary URL?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but the field’s data model, editor authorization, validation, and public trust semantics are product-policy choices rather than an established broken-behavior contract.

options.title: Add constrained organization GitHub handles
options.body: Store an optional normalized GitHub handle for organizations, render it only as public profile metadata, and retain the current handle-derived link when absent.

options.title: Allow a general public URL
options.body: Support an arbitrary organization website or GitHub URL, accepting broader validation and a less specific public contract.

options.title: Keep handle-derived links only
options.body: Decline separate public identity metadata and require organizations to use matching ClawHub and GitHub handles.

recommendation.title: Add constrained organization GitHub handles
recommendation.body: Store an optional normalized GitHub handle for organizations, render it only as public profile metadata, and retain the current handle-derived link when absent.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete mismatch case and can clarify the intended organization-publisher workflow while a repository product owner chooses the permanent contract.
